core_obligations: Show that the action of O' on I factors through O because I has square zero, which gives I the structure of a sheaf of O-modules and hence M the structure of an R-module (proof lines 5755-5758).

Reduce the derivation property to the Leibniz rule, since the boundary map is additive, and represent the boundary class of f by the Cech cocycle f_i - f_j for a covering along which f lifts locally (proof lines 5759-5767).

Verify the Leibniz rule by computation: with beta the cocycle of g, the cocycle gamma of the product has entries f_{i_0}g_{i_0} - f_{i_1}g_{i_1} = alpha_{i_0i_1} g + f beta_{i_0i_1}, which is exactly the asserted identity (proof lines 5768-5781).
proof_roadmap: Get the module structures from the square zero condition (proof lines 5755-5758).
Represent the boundary classes by Cech cocycles (proof lines 5759-5767).
Compute the cocycle of a product (proof lines 5768-5781).
difficulty_reason: Let O' to O be a surjection of sheaves of rings with square zero kernel I; the lemma shows that M = H^1(X, I) is a module over R = H^0(X, O) and that the boundary map R to M of the associated short exact sequence is a derivation (statement lines 5741-5752). The proof first observes that the conjugation map of O' into the sheaf of endomorphisms of I factors through O because the square of I vanishes, which gives both the O-module structure on I and hence the R-module structure on M (proof lines 5755-5758). Additivity being automatic, the author verifies the Leibniz rule explicitly: lift f and g locally along a covering, write the boundary classes as first Cech cocycles f_i - f_j and g_i - g_j with respect to that covering, and compute the cocycle of the product as the sum of the two terms, exactly as the Leibniz rule requires (proof lines 5759-5780). The claim is H2: the content is one algebraic observation plus a concrete cocycle computation, both written out in full.
